title: RAF Ingham — Polish Bomber Squadrons Memorial Centre
memorial_type: Memorial centre — large kerbed gravel area with three memorial stones and four flagpoles
memorial_address: Polish Bomber Squadrons Centre, RAF Ingham, Fillingham, West Lindsey, Lincolnshire
erected_by: Lord Lieutenant of Lincolnshire + representatives from Polish Consulate
inscription: Za Waska wolnose i nasza (For Your Freedom and Ours)
narrative: RAF Ingham near Fillingham in Lincolnshire was home to Polish and British bomber squadrons during World War Two. The Polish Bomber Squadrons Memorial Centre was opened on 17 April 2024 — one of the most recent major Bomber Command memorials in England — with the Lord Lieutenant of Lincolnshire and representatives from the Polish Consulate in attendance. The memorial covers 300 (Masovia) and 305 (Ziemia Wielopolska) Squadrons of the Polish Air Force, as well as 199 Squadron RAF. A large kerbed gravel area holds three memorial stones and four flagpoles flying the flags of the United Kingdom, Poland, Australia, and Canada. The left stone bears the RAF badge alongside the badges of 199, 300, and 305 Squadrons. The centre stone records the 166 names of those who died. The right stone carries the Polish Air Force badge and a dedication to all four Polish bomber squadrons. The motto 'Za Waska wolnose i nasza' — For Your Freedom and Ours — was the rallying call of the exiled Polish forces who fought on despite losing their homeland.
memorial_details: Large kerbed gravel area with three memorial stones and four flagpoles (UK, Poland, Australia, Canada). Left stone: RAF badge + 199/300/305 Squadron badges. Centre stone: 166 names of those who died. Right stone: Polish Air Force badge + dedication to four Polish bomber squadrons. Opened 17 April 2024 — a very recent addition to the Bomber Memorial Record. IWM War Memorials Register reference: IWM 108566.
